text: The assumptions presented in the context of estimating turkey cooking time—specifically that the oven temperature remains constant, the turkey has uniform density, and it is fully defrosted—are simplifications used to make the mathematical modeling of heat transfer tractable. In reality, these assumptions do not strictly comply with physical and mathematical principles because oven temperatures fluctuate, turkey density varies by tissue type (bone, muscle, fat), and defrosting is rarely perfectly uniform. However, in applied mathematics, such idealizations are necessary to create solvable differential equations for heat conduction, acknowledging that the resulting model is an approximation rather than an exact representation of physical reality.
